title: Choosing songs for 'Closest Pages in the Book'
summary: Her album with Wilber, including 're-recording 'Gone With the Wind', 'Darn That Dream' and 'Too Many Tears'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Anyway, so a few months later, that led to an album on which you appear all the way through, which was recorded on the 11th and 13th of June, 1969.
Yeah.
The title is 'Closest Pages In The Book,' and the album is out under your name and Bob Wilber's (both, I'd).
Right.
Again, it's on the Monmouth-Evergreen label.

Well, these were tunes that I selected to do. Most of them were standards -- pretty standard.
I got a chance to record 'Gone With The Wind' again -- 'Gone With The Wind' having been my first recording, but nobody knew about it, I supposed.
Most people talk about 'Loch Lomond' actually as though it was your first --
That's right.
They're missing out on something goo.

And, of course, I got a chance to do 'Darn That Dream' on the album. And 'Darn That Dream' was one of the selections that I introduced when we did the swing version of Midsummer Night's Dream. It was from Swinging the Dream. (Inaudible).
Was the song written for that show?
Yes, it was written for that show.
I didn't know that.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah.
That's a favorite of mine.

And 'Too Many Tears' is a real old song. I remember having heard 'Too Many Tears' years ago in Homestead when I was a youngster. We had a theater in Homestead, Pennsylvania that had live stage productions. And I remember a scene where they had some penguins -- they weren't penguins, but they were midgets. I think it was singing midgets. And they were dressed as penguins. And they marched across the stage to 'Too Many Tears.' I don't know why unless it was because 'Too Many Tears' was sort of a slow song. But I had remembered that, and I wanted to sing that. 'Restless' was an oldie. I don't know who I heard sing that years ago, but I --
Well the classic version, as I recall, is Helen Ward with the Benny Goodman Band.
Yes.
